payload.rationale: Both sides debated at a high level with consistent citation, clean rebuttal-then-extend structure, and disciplined clash, so the margin is narrow. CON anchored on a single durable metric (IMDb Top 250 #1) plus a resonance/universality framing, and scored its cleanest win by neutralizing PRO's National Film Registry 'timing/charter-member' hierarchy: CON cited the Library of Congress's own statement that the Registry is not a ranking and that induction tracks 10-year eligibility windows and a 25-title cap, exposing PRO's repeated 'cornerstone vs. later addition' claim as rhetoric, not institutional fact. That is a textbook refute-with-citation win (Principle 3). However, PRO carried the decisive exchanges. PRO turned CON's IMDb anchor by noting The Godfather sits at #2 on the very same list — establishing rough parity among the popular crowd and forcing the tiebreak onto expert/critical consensus, the arena CON itself conceded was the better test of greatness. There PRO held concrete, side-by-side evidence (AFI #2 vs. Shawshank #72 on the same 2007 ballot, both eligible; Sight & Sound inclusion vs. absence; the 1973 Best Picture/Actor/Screenplay sweep vs. Shawshank's 0-for-7). CON answered only by impugning the AFI jury as a 'clubby guild' and asserting age-bias, but never produced a competing expert ranking placing Shawshank above The Godfather, and conceded NFR co-membership establishes only peerage, not superiority. Under Principle 4, PRO's AFI rank-gap and craft-convergence (Brando, three supporting nominees, Willis, Rota) went under-answered for multiple turns and largely stand, while the influence line was mutually washed via the Birth of a Nation analogy. PRO's framing — greatness as the union of moving audiences AND reshaping the form, with CON conceding the latter to The Godfather — proved the more complete burden discharge.
payload.persuasion_notes: Principle 2 (clash) decides this: PRO directly engaged and turned CON's central IMDb evidence every round, whereas CON, after its strong cited takedown of the NFR-timing point (Principle 3, properly sourced), could only attack the AFI jury's legitimacy without supplying a rival expert verdict — a warrant attack that ends in a 'wash,' which does not win the tiebreak CON needed. Principle 4 (dropped arguments stand) favors PRO: the AFI 70-rank gap and the ensemble-craft case were never overturned. Principle 1 (persuasion not truth): CON's emotional 'authored hope' rhetoric was the more affecting prose, but PRO conceded that affection while showing it was necessary-not-sufficient, leaving PRO holding both crowd-parity and uncontested expert consensus. Higher Clash and fewer dropped claims both break to PRO (Principle 5).
